appearance.organs.leaf.shape.template.why: A monocot's uncut linear leaf is mostly leaf base, sessile and sheathing (Kaplan): drawn as a strap on the blade card; otherwise as at the flowering plants, a compound, palmate, lobed or simple card.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.template.why: A monocot's uncut linear leaf is mostly leaf base, sessile and sheathing (Kaplan): drawn as a strap on the blade card; otherwise as at the flowering plants, a compound, palmate, lobed or simple card.

appearance.organs.basal_piece.shape.temp.why: The pieces of a monocot's arching strap leaf are blades, as its tip is; other leaves draw as at the flowering plants.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.aspect.why: A strap leaf is as wide for its length as its flora measures it; where it gives no measures, 1 in 25, a linear monocot leaf's.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.aspect.why: Each piece of an arching strap leaf is as wide as the leaf, for the piece's length: the leaf's width over its length, as its flora measures it (else 1 in 25), times its pieces.

appearance.organs.basal_piece.shape.aspe.why: Each piece of an arching strap leaf is as wide as the leaf, for the piece's length: the leaf's width over its length, as its flora measures it (else 1 in 25), times its pieces.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.taper.why: A strap leaf narrows to its tip in its last piece.

appearance.organs.basal_piece.shape.tape.why: The pieces below a strap leaf's tip keep its width.

generator.params.basal_pieces.why: A linear basal leaf arches in four pieces, as the curated camas, iris and blue-eyed grass do.

generator.params.basal_arch.why: Its pieces bend 10 degrees at each joint, the middle of the curated camas's, iris's and blue-eyed grass's (5 to 14).

generator.params.basal_length.why: A basal leaf is as long as floras measure the leaves.

generator.params.scape.why: A flowering stem without leaves is drawn as a leafless scape above the leaves at its foot.

appearance.organs.leaf.roll.why: A unifacial sword leaf is borne edgewise to the stem, its faces in the plane of its fan: its card turns a quarter turn about its length.

appearance.organs.basal.roll.why: A unifacial sword leaf is borne edgewise to the stem, its faces in the plane of its fan: its card turns a quarter turn about its length.

appearance.organs.basal_piece.roll.why: A unifacial sword leaf is borne edgewise to the stem, its faces in the plane of its fan: its card turns a quarter turn about its length.

traits.note: Hutchinson's conspectus of the flowering plants (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959): the monocotyledons' leaves are typically parallel-nerved and alternate, and their flowers usually in threes. Net-veined leaves (yams, aroids) and whorled or opposite ones (Trillium, Paris) are the exceptions, which their families state.

traits.perianth.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) pp. 7, 46, 355: the monocot perianth is two whorls of three like, usually petaloid tepals; a few families (Commelinaceae, Bromeliaceae) set a green calyx apart from a coloured corolla.

traits.stamens.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) pp. 88, 355: the monocot flower is very constantly P3+3 A3+3 G3, two whorls of three stamens; families that lose a whorl (Iridaceae 3) or more (orchids, gingers 1) state their own.

traits.carpels.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) pp. 88, 355: three carpels, joined, in the constant monocot plan P3+3 A3+3 G3.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.shape.templ.note: Kaplan (2022, pp. 391-397): in many monocots the leaf's upper zone is only a tiny tip and the lower zone makes the sheath and the blade, so the leaf is sessile, sheathing and parallel-veined, with no petiole; a petiole-like stalk, where there is one (Araceae, Zingiberales), is a pseudopetiole of the leaf base. Drawing a linear one as an arching strap on the blade card is the model's choice (visual forms Skill 5, 2026-10-15).

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.roll.note: Kaplan (2022, pp. 374-385): unifacial leaves (radial in section above a bifacial sheathing base) are either round (Allium, many Juncus) or flattened in the median plane as sword leaves (Iris, Gladiolus, Moraea, Sisyrinchium, Acorus), held edgewise to the stem. Turning a card a quarter turn about its length draws a flat sword leaf so, a choice of the model's (visual forms Skill 5, 2026-10-15); a round one waits for a round card.
